text: Something deceptive gives you the wrong idea, even without a lie. The fancy menu words make the plain meal sound grand.
To improvise is to make do on the spot with whatever you have. The passenger uses a knife and a spoon because he has no proper way to scoop the salad.
Gingerly means very carefully and gently, like walking on a slippery floor. The passenger moves the lid slowly because the tray is so crowded.
A crew member is one of the people who work on the plane, like the flight attendants who serve the food.
An airline is a company that flies passengers from place to place in planes.
A menu is a list of the foods you can choose from. On a plane the choice is usually only two or three things.
Seasonal means connected to a certain time of year, like soup in winter or watermelon in summer. On a menu it is a fancy word that sounds fresh.
A vinaigrette is a salad dressing made from oil and vinegar. Here it comes in a tiny packet.
Herb-encrusted means covered with a coating of chopped green herbs like parsley. It is menu language meant to sound fancy.
Jus is a French word, said like zhoo, for a thin sauce made from meat juices. It is another fancy menu word.
Basque cheesecake is a creamy cake from the Basque region of Spain, with a dark, burnt-looking top.
A sachet is a small, flat packet that holds a bit of something, like salad dressing or sugar.
Vacuum-packed means sealed in plastic with the air sucked out, so food stays fresh and the wrapping fits tightly.
A ripple is a small wave, like the ones on a pond. Here it means a tiny feeling of excitement that spreads through you.
Ritualised means done the same way every time, like a ceremony. Airline meals follow a set order, so they feel like a ritual.
Your critical faculties are your ability to think clearly and judge things well. The joke is that thin air might be making the writer too easy to please.
An aperitif is a small drink served before a meal. The word is French.
Pretzels are crunchy, salty snacks, often shaped like a knot.
What's not to like? is a saying that means everything about this seems good. It is a joking way to say it is an easy choice.
Dining is a formal word for eating a meal. The crew member's question is funny because there is nowhere else on a plane to eat.
Absurdly means in a silly way that makes no sense. Of course you are dining with them, because you are stuck on the plane.
A wintry smile is a cold, quick smile with no warmth, like a chilly winter day.
A luxury is something extra nice that you do not really need and that costs more. The joke is that a plate counts as one.
Aviation is the business and science of flying aircraft.
Remarkable means worth noticing because it is surprising or unusual.
Deposited means put down in a place, often without much care. The tray is simply set on your table.
A fiesta is a big, lively party. Here, a fiesta of plastic means the tray is crowded with plastic pieces, a joke.
A sliding-block puzzle is a game where small tiles slide around in a tight frame until you get them in order. The tray's dishes fit together the same tight way.
Snugly means fitting tightly and neatly, with no gaps.
Retrieving means getting something back after it is lost or out of reach, like a fork that fell on the floor.
A portion is the amount of food given to one person.
Here, to apply butter means to spread it on. Apply can also mean to ask for a job, or to use a rule.
Soften means to make less hard. The writer uses wine to soften a dry roll in his mouth.
An ensemble is a group of things that go together, like a band or an outfit. Here it means the whole set of dishes and lids.
To balance is to keep something steady so it does not fall.
Cutlery means forks, knives, and spoons.
A casual observer is someone who glances at something without paying close attention.
Foil is a very thin sheet of shiny metal used to cover food and keep it warm.
Coastal erosion is when waves slowly wear away the land along a coast. It takes years, so cutting the chicken at that pace is very slow, which is the joke.
Whittling is cutting small bits off a piece of wood with a knife. To whittle away at something is to cut it down bit by bit.
An array is a neat group of things laid out together, like a row of bottles.
Perches means sits on the edge of something, the way a bird sits on a branch.
Majestically means in a grand, noble way. It is funny here because it describes a flying cheesecake.
Vaults means jumps over something in one big leap, like an athlete over a hurdle. Here the cheesecake leaps two rows ahead.
Overhead lockers are the storage bins above airplane seats where people put bags.
Dissecting means carefully cutting something apart to look inside, like a science class does with a specimen. Here it is a joke about cutting chicken.
Taxed means tested or stretched to the limit. If food has not taxed the taste buds, it has no flavor to speak of.
To teeter is to wobble as if about to fall.
Alexander Calder was an American artist famous for sculptures with metal pieces balanced so they sway. The tray looks like one.
To prise something is to pry it out or open with force. It is a British spelling of pry.
Snoring is the noisy breathing some people make when they sleep.
